paper_level_summary_zh: 该论文在相关工作中将目标论文列为代表性RFID穿墙窃听工作，但未提供具体的亚毫米精度或能力确认语句；引用属于普通的相关工作归类。

evidences.evidence_quote: Other studies, such as MILLIEAR [18], mmSpy [6], and mmWave-Whisper [7], focused on eavesdropping phone conversations by capturing speech radiated from smartphones.
evidences.evidence_context: Active-source attacks directly detect vibrations from the speaker or device. For example, Li et al. [28] captured screen vibrations to infer on-screen content, while WaveEar [49] recovered speech by sensing throat vibrations in noisy environments. Subsequent studies enhanced speaker recognition and speech detection using mmWave signals [13, 26]. Other studies, such as MILLIEAR [18], mmSpy [6], and mmWave-Whisper [7], focused on eavesdropping phone conversations by capturing speech radiated from smartphones. Passive-source attacks, by contrast, extract secondary vibrations from nearby objects. Radiomic [35] proposed reconstructing speech via micro-vibrations on non-contact surfaces. mmPhone [41] augmented sensing with piezoelectric films to address weak vibration scenarios. mmEcho [17] departed from learning-based methods, instead using signal processing to recover intelligible speech from radar reflections off everyday indoor objects.
